seoDescription: Learn how to elevate your weaving projects by transforming a standard diamond twill pattern into a beautiful two-color design. This tutorial guides you through adapting a weaving chart for two colors, showing you how to handle multiple weft yarns within the same row to create stunning, contrasted diamonds. Discover tips on yarn selection, such as using chunky yarns like Loops & Threads Lush Alpaca and Lion Brand Thick & Quick, and loom setup for optimal results on your tapestry weaving.

summary:
## Core Concept: Adapting Diamond Twill

The fundamental idea is to take a standard, single-color diamond twill pattern and adapt it for two colors. This is achieved by coloring in the pattern chart to designate which sections will be woven with a light color and which with a dark color, creating contrast that highlights the diamond shapes.

> [!TIP]
> A free PDF of the exact pattern used in this tutorial is available by signing up for the email list at **sprucenlinen.com**.

## Materials & Setup
- **Yarn**: Chunky weight yarn is recommended for this pattern.
  - **Dark Color**: Loops & Threads Lush Alpaca
  - **Light Color**: Lion Brand Thick & Quick
- **Loom**: A loom with **5 ends per inch (EPI)**, like the Becca loom used here, works better for this technique than a wider sett.
- **Warp**: The loom is warped with **27 warp strings** to match the pattern chart exactly.

## Reading the Two-Color Chart
- **Colored-in squares** = **Over** that warp string.
- **Empty squares** = **Under** that warp string.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Any pattern row containing **both colors is treated as two separate weaving passes**. First, you weave only the blocks designated for one color. Then, on the same row, you make a second pass with the other color, weaving only its designated blocks.

## Weaving Technique

- **Use a Guide**: Cover the rows above and below the one you are working on with a piece of paper to avoid getting lost in the pattern.
- **Multiple Needles**: Using two separate tapestry needles (one for each color) makes the process much smoother.
- **Clean Edges**: When switching colors, don't wrap the unused yarn around the edge warp string. Instead, let it hang at the back and simply bring it up from behind when it's needed again. This prevents messy, bulky edges.
- **Pattern Repeat**: After completing the full 14-row pattern block, the repeat doesn't start back at row 1. Due to the two-color passes, the pattern continues from row 3 to maintain the sequence.

## Tips for Success
- **Don't Beat Too Hard**: Gently press the weft rows into place with your fingers or a weaving comb. Beating the yarn down too firmly will compress the pattern and obscure the diamond shapes.
- **Contrast is Key**: For the most dramatic effect, use a warp color that contrasts strongly with both of your weft colors. A black warp, for instance, would make the pattern even more pronounced.
- **Expect Long Floats**: The back of the weaving will have long floats (loops of yarn) where a color had to travel under many warp strings. This is a normal and expected result of this technique.
